chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from some of his companions, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Sulayman ibn Ziyad al-Tamimi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'The close one is he whom affection has brought near, even if his lineage is distant; and the distant one is he whom affection has driven away, even if his lineage is near. There is nothing closer to something than a hand is to the body; and yet the hand, if it becomes treacherous, is cut off — and when cut off, the bleeding is stopped.'

key_terms.الْقَرِيبُ / الْبَعِيدُ: Al-qarib / al-ba'id — the close one / the distant one; here redefined from genealogical to relational proximity
key_terms.الْمَوَدَّةُ: Mawadda — affection, cordiality, warm bond of loyalty; stronger than mere friendship
key_terms.تَغُلُّ: Taghlul — to be treacherous, to act with ghulul (betrayal/embezzlement); the same root implies betrayal of trust
key_terms.نَسَبُ: Nasab — lineage, blood descent; the traditional basis of Arab tribal kinship

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Hasan say about closeness and distance among people?
ai.summary: Imam al-Hasan ibn Ali (AS), as transmitted by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), teaches that true closeness and distance among people is defined by affection and loyalty, not blood lineage. He illustrates this with a striking analogy: as intimate as a hand is to the body, if the hand becomes treacherous, it is amputated — demonstrating that betrayal severs even the closest bond. This teaching challenges tribal Arab notions of kinship, reorienting the community toward bonds of sincere loyalty.
